Fit a Multi-Seasonal ARIMA Model

Source: R/msarima.R
msarima.Rd

Fits an ARIMA model with one or more seasonal components to a univariate time series. This function extends the standard ARIMA framework to time series with several seasonal patterns, such as daily and weekly seasonality in hourly data, or weekly and yearly seasonality in daily data.

Usage

msarima(
  y,
  order = c(0, 0, 0),
  seasonal = list(),
  seasonal.period = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  include.constant = FALSE,
  optim_control = list(maxit = 200)
)

Arguments

y

A numeric vector or time series object (ts or msts) containing the data to be modelled. If y is a ts object and seasonal.period is not supplied, its frequency is used as the first seasonal period; if y is an msts object, its seasonal periods are used. Missing values are not allowed.

order

A numeric vector of length 3 specifying the non-seasonal part of the ARIMA model: the AR order (p), the degree of differencing (d), and the MA order (q). Default is c(0, 0, 0).

seasonal

A list of numeric vectors, each of length 3, specifying the seasonal components. Each vector gives the seasonal AR order (P), the seasonal differencing order (D), and the seasonal MA order (Q) of one component. For example, list(c(1, 0, 1), c(0, 1, 1)) specifies two seasonal components. Use list() for a model without seasonal components. Default is list().

seasonal.period

A numeric vector of seasonal periods, one for each element of seasonal, for example c(7, 30) for weekly and monthly seasonality. If NULL, the periods are taken from y when it is a ts or msts object. Periods can be given in any order but must be distinct. Default is NULL.

fixed

A numeric vector with one entry per parameter, used to hold some of them at a given value: only the NA entries are estimated. The parameters are ordered as non-seasonal AR, seasonal AR (one block per seasonal component), non-seasonal MA, seasonal MA (one block per seasonal component), sigma, and the constant term when include.constant = TRUE. Default is NULL, meaning that all parameters are estimated.

include.constant

Should the model include a constant term? The constant is the intercept of the model equation, not the mean of the series: for a stationary model the two are related by \(\mu = c / \phi(1)\), where \(c\) is the intercept and \(\phi(1)\) is the full AR polynomial (seasonal components included) evaluated at 1. For example, for an AR(1) model \(\mu = c / (1 - \phi_1)\). A constant cannot be combined with differencing and is dropped, with a warning, when d or any D is non-zero. Default is FALSE.

optim_control

A list of control parameters passed to optim. Default is list(maxit = 200).

Value

An object of class "msarima", which is a list containing:

order

The non-seasonal ARIMA order (p, d, q).

seasonal

List of seasonal orders (P, D, Q), one vector per seasonal component.

seasonal.period

Vector of seasonal periods.

coef

Named vector of estimated coefficients: the AR, SAR, MA and SMA parameters, followed by the intercept if include.constant = TRUE.

var_coef

Variance-covariance matrix of the coefficient estimates, with the same dimension and order as coef. Rows and columns of fixed parameters are NA.

mask

Logical vector with the same length and order as coef, TRUE for fixed parameters.

loglik

Log-likelihood of the fitted model.

aic

Akaike Information Criterion.

bic

Bayesian Information Criterion.

aicc

Corrected Akaike Information Criterion.

sigma2

Estimated innovation variance.

x

The original time series.

fitted

One-step-ahead fitted values, on the scale of the original series.

residuals

Model residuals. Together with fitted, the first d + sum(D * S) values are NA, since differencing leaves no observations to predict for them.

method

Character string describing the fitted model, e.g. "mSARIMA(1,0,0)(1,0,0)[4]".

series

Name of the series.

nobs

Number of observations in the original series.

n.used

Number of observations used in estimation (after differencing).

call

The matched call.

convergence

Convergence code from optim (0 indicates successful convergence).

Details

The model is estimated by conditional maximum likelihood: the residuals are computed recursively and the resulting Gaussian log-likelihood is maximised numerically with optim, using the BFGS algorithm.

When d or any D is non-zero, the series is differenced before estimation and the ARMA part is estimated on the differenced data. The first d + sum(D * S) observations are therefore not used, which is why the residuals and the fitted values start with as many NA values: these observations have no differenced value to predict, so no residual is defined for them under the conditional likelihood.

Standard errors are computed from the inverse of the observed information matrix (negative Hessian). If the Hessian is singular, a warning is issued and the standard errors are set to NA.

Note

  • The series must have at least 10 observations, both before and after differencing.

  • Seasonal periods must be at least 2 and at most half the length of the series.

  • If y is a ts or msts object, x, fitted and residuals keep the same time series structure. If y is a plain numeric vector, they are returned as ts with one seasonal period, or as msts with several.

Examples

# Example 1: ARIMA with two seasonal components
set.seed(123)
y <- msarima.sim(nsim = 200,
                 order = c(1, 0, 0),
                 seasonal = list(c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 1)),
                 seasonal.period = c(4, 11),
                 ar = c(0.5, 0.5), ma = 0.3, sigma2 = 1)

fit <- msarima(y, order = c(1, 0, 0),
               seasonal = list(c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 1)),
               seasonal.period = c(4, 11))
print(fit)
#> Series: y 
#> mSARIMA(1,0,0)(1,0,0)[4](0,0,1)[11]
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>    AR(1) SAR(1,1) SMA(2,1) 
#>   0.4101   0.4678   0.3805 
#> 
#> sigma^2 = 0.9272  log likelihood = -92.44
#> AIC = 192.88   AICc = 193.08   BIC = 206.07
summary(fit)
#> Series: y 
#> mSARIMA(1,0,0)(1,0,0)[4](0,0,1)[11]
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>          Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> AR(1)     0.41006    0.06570   6.241 4.35e-10 ***
#> SAR(1,1)  0.46782    0.06428   7.278 3.40e-13 ***
#> SMA(2,1)  0.38051    0.06943   5.481 4.24e-08 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> sigma^2 = 0.9272  log likelihood = -92.4387
#> AIC = 192.8775   AICc = 193.0826   BIC = 206.0707

# Example 2: msts input, seasonal periods detected automatically
y_msts <- msts(y, seasonal.periods = c(4, 11))
fit_msts <- msarima(y_msts, order = c(1, 0, 0),
                    seasonal = list(c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 1)))

# Example 3: differencing
fit_diff <- msarima(cumsum(y), order = c(1, 1, 0),
                    seasonal = list(c(0, 0, 1)),
                    seasonal.period = 4)
head(residuals(fit_diff))  # the first residual is NA
#>         Qtr1       Qtr2       Qtr3       Qtr4
#> 1         NA -0.7053174 -2.4672228 -0.1094124
#> 2  0.4100991 -2.0204887                      

# Example 4: fixing parameters
# Note: the length of 'fixed' must match AR + SAR + MA + SMA + sigma
fit_fixed <- msarima(y, order = c(1, 0, 0),
                     seasonal = list(c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 1)),
                     seasonal.period = c(4, 11),
                     fixed = c(0.5, NA, NA, NA))
AIC(fit); AIC(fit_fixed)
#> [1] 192.8775
#> [1] 192.7455
